Coverage is narrower than GDPR because it centers on sanction decisions by the authority’s committee and lacks the “without prejudice” clause and the “effective” qualifier.

It does not provide a general objection right to all processing based on public interest or legitimate interests, nor the GDPR-specific condition of “grounds relating to the data subject’s particular situation,” and it lacks an “at any time” qualifier. The cited phrase “أي حالات أخرى تحددها اللائحة التنفيذية” appears in Art. 15 regarding erasure exceptions and does not broaden the objection right, while Art. 18 has been incorporated here as a counterpart for objection to profiling via automated decision-making.

reasoning_note: KSA Art. 17(4) addresses processor responsibility when it violates the controller’s instructions or contract, even deeming it a controller, but it does not establish liability for damages to data subjects. The GDPR rule also triggers liability when the processor breaches processor-specific obligations; KSA imposes such obligations (e.g., Art. 17(5)) but does not textually link their breach to damages liability. This yields only partial alignment, with a narrower trigger and no express damages remedy.

The combination approximates the GDPR obligation but lacks an explicit mandatory duty to take all necessary measures specifically to ensure penalties are implemented.
